title: Writing Task 2: Problem and Solution
topic: Menjelaskan masalah, penyebab, akibat, dan solusi yang realistis
objectives: Menjelaskan penyebab dan akibat dari sebuah masalah
Menilai solusi dengan kata yang tepat
Membedakan solusi yang menangani gejala dan penyebab

keywords: IELTS writing task 2 problem solution essay

lesson.intro: Esai problem and solution menjelaskan masalah, menganalisis penyebab dan akibatnya, lalu mengusulkan solusi. Solusi yang kuat menangani sumber masalah dan menyebut bagaimana hasilnya bisa diukur.

sections.heading: Masalah dan penyebab
sections.bodyMd: Jelaskan **problem** dengan jelas, lalu sebut **cause** utamanya. Pisahkan penyebab dari **effect** agar pembaca tidak bingung.

sections.heading: Solusi
sections.bodyMd: Gunakan **tackle** atau **address** untuk menangani masalah. Gunakan **prevent** untuk mencegah dan **mitigate** untuk mengurangi dampak. Sebut **initiative** jika ada program nyata.

sections.heading: Keterbatasan
sections.bodyMd: Akui bahwa tidak ada satu solusi yang sempurna. Gunakan kata **remedy** untuk menunjukkan obat atau perbaikan, dan **fix** untuk hal yang bisa diperbaiki langsung.

block3.title: Banjir di Kawasan Bawah Kota
block3.text:
Every year, heavy rain causes serious flooding in the lower part of the city. The problem is not new, but it has grown worse over the last decade. Residents report damaged homes, closed schools, and long delays on the main road. Understanding the causes is the first step toward a real fix.

The main cause is the loss of open land. Many fields near the river have been covered with concrete, so rainwater cannot soak into the ground. Instead, water flows quickly into the drains, which are often too narrow for the volume. The effect is a sudden rise in water levels within a few hours.

Some people argue that the drains alone should be enlarged. This would address one symptom, but it would not tackle the underlying problem. Larger drains only move the water faster, and the water then floods the next neighbourhood downstream. A better approach must reduce the amount of runoff at its source.

Several solutions have been proposed. Planting trees and restoring wetlands can help to mitigate the impact of storms by absorbing water. Green roofs and permeable pavements can also prevent some runoff from reaching the drains. In addition, the council has launched a community initiative in which schools and volunteers create small rain gardens.

Experts agree that no single measure is a complete remedy. The most effective strategy combines new drainage with natural solutions. The drains can handle extreme events, while the green areas reduce the everyday pressure on the system. Such a combination is more costly at first, but it reduces long-term damage.

The council should begin with the most flood-prone streets, where the risk is highest. A clear plan with measurable targets would help residents follow the progress. If the city acts now, it can prevent the worst effects of the next storm season and restore confidence in its infrastructure.

Residents also have a role to play. Households can collect rainwater in barrels, clear leaves from drains, and avoid covering gardens with paving. These small actions add up, especially when many people take part in them together. Schools that join the programme can also teach pupils how water moves through a neighbourhood, so that the next generation understands the problem and helps to prevent it.
